expression: As soon as I texted her, she called me back.
situation: 어떤 일이 일어나자마자 곧바로 다른 일이 이어졌다고 말할 때
nuance: as soon as 가 '~하자마자'의 핵심. 두 사건이 거의 동시에 일어난 느낌을 강조한다.
example_1: As soon as I got home, it started raining.
example_2: As soon as the movie ended, everyone stood up.

expression: Don't wait up for me.
situation: 늦게 귀가할 때 가족이나 룸메이트에게 미리 일러둘 때
nuance: wait up = 자지 않고 기다리다. 배려가 담긴 다정한 말투다.
example_1: I'll be home late tonight, so don't wait up for me.
example_2: Go to bed early — don't wait up.

expression: He's really passionate about organizing.
situation: 누가 어떤 일에 푹 빠져 열정적일 때
nuance: be passionate about ~ = ~에 열정적이다. 요즘 말 '진심이야'와 통하는 느낌.
example_1: She's really passionate about the environment.
example_2: He's passionate about cooking — he watches recipe videos all day.

expression: I can tell when something's wrong.
translation_ko: 뭔가 잘못됐을 때 난 바로 알아채
situation: 분위기나 상대의 상태 변화를 눈치챈다고 말할 때
nuance: can tell = (보거나 느껴서) 알아채다. 직감적으로 안다는 뉘앙스.
example_1: I can tell you're tired just by looking at you.
example_2: She could tell something was off the moment she walked in.

expression: I can't see myself living in Seoul.
translation_ko: 서울에서 사는 건 상상이 안 돼
situation: 어떤 미래를 자신과 연결지어 상상하기 어려울 때
nuance: can't see myself -ing = 내가 ~하는 모습이 그려지지 않는다. 완곡한 회의에도 쓴다.
example_1: I can't see myself working here in ten years.
example_2: Honestly, I can't see myself getting married anytime soon.

expression: I don't really care about money.
situation: 자신의 가치관을 가볍게 밝힐 때
nuance: don't care about = 신경 쓰지 않다. really 를 넣으면 단정적이지 않고 부드러워진다.
example_1: I don't really care about brands.
example_2: He doesn't care about what people think.

expression: I don't follow sports.
situation: 관심 분야가 아니라고 말할 때
nuance: follow = (관심 갖고) 챙겨 보다/팔로우하다. '안 본다'를 자연스럽게 표현.
example_1: I don't really follow politics.
example_2: She follows tennis but not soccer.

expression: I doubt it.
situation: 상대의 말에 회의적으로 반응할 때
nuance: 짧지만 '그럴 것 같지 않다'는 강한 의심. 단독으로 자주 쓴다.
example_1: Will he show up on time? I doubt it.
example_2: I doubt she even remembers me.

expression: I found out.
situation: 몰랐던 사실을 알아냈을 때
nuance: find out = (없던 정보를) 알아내다/알게 되다. 이미 아는 know 와 구별된다.
example_1: I found out he'd been lying the whole time.
example_2: How did you find out about the party?

expression: I never buy pants unless I can try them on first.
translation_ko: 난 입어보지 않고는 바지 절대 안 사
situation: 자신의 확고한 습관이나 원칙을 말할 때
nuance: unless = ~하지 않는 한. never ... unless 로 '예외 없는 원칙'을 강조한다.
example_1: I never make a decision unless I've slept on it.
example_2: He won't sign anything unless his lawyer reads it first.

expression: I thought hard about what to say.
translation_ko: 무슨 말을 해야 할지 한참 고민했어
situation: 어떤 말을 꺼내기 전 신중히 고민했음을 말할 때
nuance: think hard about = 곰곰이 깊이 생각하다. 'what to + 동사'(무엇을 ~할지)와 자주 결합.
example_1: I had to think hard about whether to take the job.
example_2: Think hard before you reply to that message.

expression: I'll do everything I can to make it a success.
translation_ko: 성공할 수 있게 내가 할 수 있는 건 다 할게
situation: 어떤 일에 최선을 다하겠다고 다짐할 때
nuance: everything I can = 할 수 있는 모든 것. make it a success 처럼 'make + 목적어 + 명사' 구조.
example_1: I'll do everything I can to help you move.
example_2: We did everything we could to save the business.

expression: I'm a planner.
situation: 자신의 성향을 한마디로 소개할 때
nuance: I'm a + 명사 로 성향을 간단히 규정. planner = 계획 세우는 걸 좋아하는 사람.
example_1: I'm a morning person.
example_2: She's a perfectionist, so she double-checks everything.

expression: I'm really tired today for some reason.
situation: 특별한 이유 없이 컨디션이 안 좋을 때
nuance: for some reason = 왠지/이유는 모르겠지만. '이상하게도'의 느낌을 준다.
example_1: For some reason, I can't focus today.
example_2: He seemed upset for some reason.

expression: I'm sorry, but I'm going to have to say no.
situation: 부탁이나 제안을 정중하게 거절할 때
nuance: be going to have to = (어쩔 수 없이) ~해야 할 것 같다. 완곡하고 정중한 거절.
example_1: I'm going to have to cancel our meeting.
example_2: I'm afraid I'm going to have to disagree.

expression: It doesn't take much time.
situation: 어떤 일이 오래 걸리지 않는다고 안심시킬 때
nuance: take + 시간 = 시간이 걸리다. not much = 별로 ~않다.
example_1: It won't take long, I promise.
example_2: Setting it up takes no time at all.

expression: Let it go.
situation: 사소한 일에 계속 연연하는 상대에게
nuance: let it go = (붙잡지 말고) 놓아주다/잊다. 위로나 충고로 쓴다.
example_1: It's not worth it — just let it go.
example_2: I know it's hard, but you have to let it go.

expression: My book comes out in September.
situation: 책·영화·앨범 등의 출시 일정을 말할 때
nuance: come out = (작품이) 출시되다/나오다. 정해진 미래 일정에 현재시제를 자주 쓴다.
example_1: The new iPhone comes out next week.
example_2: Her album came out last month.

expression: Something's wrong with my sandwich.
situation: 음식이나 물건, 기계가 이상하다고 느낄 때
nuance: something's wrong with ~ = ~에 뭔가 문제가 있다. 콕 집지 않고 '이상함'을 표현.
example_1: Something's wrong with my laptop — it keeps freezing.
example_2: Is something wrong with the Wi-Fi?

expression: They told me to figure it out on my own.
situation: 도움 없이 혼자 해결하라는 말을 들었을 때
nuance: on my own = 혼자 힘으로. figure out = (방법을) 알아내다/해결하다.
example_1: My boss told me to handle it on my own.
example_2: I learned to cook on my own.

expression: This isn't going to change my mind.
situation: 설득에도 입장이 확고함을 보일 때
nuance: change one's mind = 마음을 바꾸다. be going to 부정으로 단호함을 더한다.
example_1: Nothing you say is going to change my mind.
example_2: I changed my mind — let's stay in tonight.

expression: This wasn't part of the plan.
situation: 예상 밖의 일이 벌어졌을 때
nuance: part of the plan = 계획의 일부. 예정에 없던 변수에 대해 쓴다.
example_1: Getting stuck here overnight wasn't part of the plan.
example_2: Was this part of your plan all along?

expression: We talked about my raise over lunch.
situation: 식사하면서 어떤 주제를 의논했다고 말할 때
nuance: over lunch/coffee = 점심/커피를 하면서. '~하면서'를 over 로 간결하게 표현.
example_1: Let's discuss it over coffee.
example_2: We caught up over dinner last night.

expression: We usually use Zipcar, and it's great.
translation_ko: 우린 보통 집카 쓰는데 진짜 좋아
situation: 평소 이용하는 서비스를 추천할 때
nuance: usually = 평소에. 두 절을 and 로 자연스럽게 이어 추천한다.
example_1: We usually take the subway, and it's super convenient.
example_2: I usually use this app, and it works really well.

expression: We're going to lose our table.
situation: 식당에서 예약 자리나 테이블을 놓칠 상황일 때
nuance: be going to lose ~ = (이대로면) ~를 놓치겠다. 임박한 결과를 경고.
example_1: Hurry up, or we're going to miss the train.
example_2: If we're late, we'll lose our reservation.

expression: What time do you close?
situation: 가게의 영업 마감 시간을 물을 때
nuance: close = (가게가) 문을 닫다. '몇 시에 닫나요'가 곧 '몇 시까지 해요'.
example_1: What time does the bank open?
example_2: They close at 9 on weekdays.

expression: You can't refreeze this.
situation: 한번 녹은 음식을 재냉동하면 안 된다고 말할 때
nuance: re- = 다시. refreeze, reuse 처럼 동사 앞에 붙어 '재~'의 뜻을 만든다.
example_1: You can't reuse this once it's opened.
example_2: Can I refreeze leftover soup?

expression: You didn't clean up after your dog.
situation: 반려견의 배변을 치우지 않은 사람에게
nuance: clean up after ~ = ~가 어지른 것을 치우다/뒤처리하다.
example_1: Please clean up after yourself in the kitchen.
example_2: I'm always cleaning up after my kids.

expression: You're quite the photographer.
situation: 상대의 솜씨를 가볍게 칭찬할 때
nuance: quite the + 명사 = 제법 ~인 사람. 살짝 감탄과 농담이 섞인 칭찬.
example_1: You're quite the cook!
example_2: He's quite the storyteller.

expression: You're starting to like the gym.
situation: 누가 점점 어떤 것을 좋아하게 될 때
nuance: start to like = 좋아지기 시작하다. 변화의 과정을 부드럽게 짚는다.
example_1: I'm starting to like my new job.
example_2: They're starting to get along.

expression: leave out
situation: 목록이나 이야기에서 무언가를 일부러 빼거나 깜빡 빠뜨릴 때
nuance: leave out = 포함하지 않다/빠뜨리다. 사람을 소외시킨다는 뜻으로도 쓴다.
example_1: You left out the most important part of the story.
example_2: Don't leave me out next time.

expression: look through
situation: 서류나 책을 빠르게 대강 살펴볼 때
nuance: look through = 처음부터 끝까지 쭉 훑다. 꼼꼼한 정독이 아닌 빠른 확인.
example_1: Can you look through this report before I send it?
example_2: I looked through the menu but couldn't decide.

expression: mess with
situation: 누군가를 함부로 건드리거나 시비 걸지 말라고 할 때
nuance: mess with = 시비 걸다/장난치다/함부로 다루다. 약간 거친 구어 표현.
example_1: Don't mess with my stuff.
example_2: You don't want to mess with her — she's tough.

expression: make out
situation: 잘 안 보이거나 안 들리는 것을 겨우 분간할 때
nuance: make out = 흐릿한 것을 식별해내다. 주로 부정문에서 '잘 못 알아보겠다'로 쓴다.
example_1: I couldn't make out what he was saying.
example_2: Can you make out the sign from here?

expression: make up for
situation: 실수나 부족함을 다른 것으로 메우거나 보상할 때
nuance: make up for = 부족분을 메우다. lost time, mistakes 등과 자주 결합.
example_1: Let me make up for being late — coffee's on me.
example_2: Hard work can make up for a lack of talent.

expression: How much do I need to save for a new house?
translation_ko: 새 집 사려면 얼마나 모아야 하지?
situation: 목표를 위해 돈이 얼마나 필요한지 따질 때
nuance: how much do I need to ~ = ~하려면 얼마나 필요한가. save for = ~를 위해 저축하다.
example_1: How much do we need to save for the trip?
example_2: I'm saving up for a new laptop.

expression: AI is exactly where technology is headed.
situation: 어떤 분야의 흐름이나 방향을 단언할 때
nuance: where ~ is headed = ~가 향하는 방향. exactly 로 확신을 강조한다.
example_1: Remote work is where the industry is headed.
example_2: This is exactly where I want my career to go.

expression: Apparently my emails were going to his spam folder.
translation_ko: 알고 보니 내 메일이 걔 스팸함으로 가고 있었더라
situation: 나중에 알게 된 사실을 전할 때
nuance: apparently = (듣자 하니/알고 보니) ~인 모양이다. 직접 확인하지 않은 정보에 쓴다.
example_1: Apparently, they broke up last week.
example_2: Apparently the store is closed on Mondays.

expression: Do you really want such a big wedding?
translation_ko: 결혼식 진짜 그렇게 크게 하고 싶어?
situation: 상대의 결정을 다시 생각해보게 할 때
nuance: really 로 진심을 되묻는 뉘앙스. such a + 형용사 + 명사 = 그렇게 ~한 ….
example_1: Do you really want to quit over this?
example_2: It was such a long day.

expression: Everything reminds me of our trip to New York.
translation_ko: 뭘 봐도 뉴욕 여행 생각이 나
situation: 무엇이든 어떤 추억을 떠올리게 할 때
nuance: remind me of ~ = ~를 떠올리게 하다. of 뒤에 사람·일·추억이 온다.
example_1: This song reminds me of high school.
example_2: You remind me of my brother.

expression: How I feel about her isn't important.
translation_ko: 내가 그녀를 어떻게 생각하는지는 중요하지 않아
situation: 자기 감정보다 다른 게 중요하다고 말할 때
nuance: How I feel ... 처럼 의문사절이 통째로 주어가 되어 명사처럼 문장 앞에 온다.
example_1: What he did matters more than what he said.
example_2: Why she left doesn't matter now.

expression: How much coffee do I need to survive today?
translation_ko: 오늘 버티려면 커피 얼마나 마셔야 하지?
situation: 힘든 하루를 앞두고 농담조로 엄살 부릴 때
nuance: need to survive = 버티는 데 필요하다. 과장된 유머로 피로를 표현.
example_1: How many naps do I need to survive this week?
example_2: I need at least two coffees to function.

expression: I didn't mean to interrupt the meeting.
situation: 의도치 않게 끼어들거나 실수했을 때 사과하며
nuance: didn't mean to = ~하려던 게 아니었다. 변명과 사과의 핵심 표현.
example_1: I didn't mean to hurt your feelings.
example_2: Sorry, I didn't mean to wake you.

expression: I don't know how to say goodbye.
translation_ko: 어떻게 작별 인사를 해야 할지 모르겠어
situation: 헤어짐이 아쉬워 말이 안 나올 때
nuance: how to + 동사 = ~하는 방법. don't know how to 로 막막함을 드러낸다.
example_1: I don't know how to thank you enough.
example_2: She doesn't know how to drive yet.

expression: I don't know how to swim.
situation: 배운 적이 없어 못 하는 것을 말할 때
nuance: don't know how to = (방법을 몰라서) 못 하다. can't 보다 '배운 적 없다'는 뉘앙스.
example_1: I don't know how to use this machine.
example_2: He doesn't know how to say no.

expression: I feel more productive here.
translation_ko: 여기 있으면 일이 더 잘 돼
situation: 특정 장소나 환경이 더 집중된다고 말할 때
nuance: feel + 비교급 = 더 ~하게 느껴지다. productive = 능률 있는.
example_1: I feel calmer when I'm near the ocean.
example_2: She feels more confident after the training.

expression: I handed in all the paperwork to my lawyer.
situation: 서류나 과제를 제출했다고 말할 때
nuance: hand in = 제출하다(직접 건네는 느낌). 격식 있는 submit 보다 구어적.
example_1: Did you hand in your assignment?
example_2: I handed in my resignation today.

expression: I know I'm the last person you want to see.
translation_ko: 내가 제일 보기 싫은 사람인 거 알아
situation: 상대가 나를 반기지 않을 걸 알면서 다가갈 때
nuance: the last person you want to ~ = 가장 ~하고 싶지 않은 사람. 강한 강조 표현.
example_1: He's the last person I'd ask for help.
example_2: Losing your phone is the last thing you want on a trip.

expression: I shouldn't have rushed into marrying her.
situation: 성급했던 과거의 결정을 후회할 때
nuance: shouldn't have p.p. = ~하지 말았어야 했다(후회). rush into = 성급히 ~하다.
example_1: I shouldn't have said that.
example_2: Don't rush into any big decisions.

expression: I want to explain everything, but he won't text me back.
translation_ko: 다 설명하고 싶은데 걔가 답장을 안 해
situation: 오해를 풀고 싶은데 상대가 응답이 없을 때
nuance: won't = (의지적으로) 안 하려 한다. 단순 미래가 아니라 '안 해줘'의 느낌.
example_1: I tried to apologize, but she won't listen.
example_2: The door won't open.

expression: I wouldn't buy the car if I were you.
situation: 상대에게 조심스럽게 조언할 때
nuance: If I were you = 내가 너라면(가정법). 부드러운 충고의 정석 표현.
example_1: If I were you, I'd take the offer.
example_2: I wouldn't worry about it if I were you.

expression: I wouldn't change anything about you.
translation_ko: 난 네 어떤 점도 바꾸고 싶지 않아
situation: 상대를 있는 그대로 좋아한다고 말할 때
nuance: wouldn't change a thing = 하나도 안 바꾸겠다. 애정이 담긴 표현.
example_1: I wouldn't change a thing about that trip.
example_2: Would you change anything if you could?

expression: I'll call you back later.
situation: 지금 통화가 어려워 나중에 다시 걸겠다고 할 때
nuance: call back = 다시 전화하다. later = 이따가.
example_1: Can I call you back in ten minutes?
example_2: She never called me back.

expression: If I were you, I wouldn't do that.
situation: 상대의 행동에 대해 조언할 때
nuance: 가정법 과거(If I were you)로 현재 상황을 충고. 직접 명령보다 완곡하다.
example_1: If I were you, I'd apologize first.
example_2: If I were in your shoes, I'd wait.

expression: Let me know if you need anything.
situation: 도움을 제안하며 대화를 마무리할 때
nuance: if you need anything = 뭐든 필요하면. 친절한 마무리 인사로 자주 쓴다.
example_1: Call me if you need help.
example_2: Text me if you need a ride.

expression: If your landlord treats you poorly, you need to stand up to him.
translation_ko: 집주인이 함부로 대하면 당당히 맞서야 해
situation: 부당한 대우에 굽히지 말고 맞서라고 조언할 때
nuance: stand up to = (강한 상대에게) 맞서다/대들다. 편들어 주는 stand up for 와 구별.
example_1: He finally stood up to his boss.
example_2: You have to stand up to bullies.

expression: Is this a Korean thing?
situation: 특정 나라나 집단 특유의 관습인지 물을 때
nuance: a [Nationality] thing = ~ 나라 특유의 것. 낯선 관습에 대한 가벼운 질문.
example_1: Taking your shoes off inside — is that a Korean thing?
example_2: Splitting the bill evenly is such a Dutch thing.

expression: It's an American thing.
situation: 어떤 관습이 특정 나라 특유라고 설명할 때
nuance: a [Nationality] thing 의 답변형. 'A만의 것'이라고 가볍게 짚는다.
example_1: Small talk with strangers is a very American thing.
example_2: Is queuing so politely a British thing?

expression: My daughter has a great ear for music.
situation: 누가 어떤 감각이나 재능이 뛰어나다고 말할 때
nuance: have an ear for ~ = ~를 듣는 감각이 좋다. 실제 '귀'가 아닌 재능을 뜻한다.
example_1: She has a good eye for design.
example_2: He has an ear for languages.

expression: No, I'm not upset.
situation: 괜찮다고 상대를 안심시킬 때
nuance: upset = 속상한/언짢은(반드시 분노는 아님). 부드럽게 부정한다.
example_1: Are you upset with me?
example_2: Don't be upset — it's not a big deal.

expression: There's nothing left to do but wait.
situation: 할 수 있는 걸 다 하고 결과만 기다릴 때
nuance: nothing left to do but ~ = ~하는 것 말고는 남은 게 없다. but 뒤에 동사원형.
example_1: There's nothing left to do but hope for the best.
example_2: After packing, there was nothing left to do but say goodbye.

expression: She's most productive in the morning.
situation: 누가 언제 가장 집중이 잘 되는지 말할 때
nuance: most + 형용사 = 가장 ~한. 시간이나 조건과 함께 자주 쓴다.
example_1: I'm most focused late at night.
example_2: He's at his best under pressure.

expression: She's the last person you'd want to tell a secret to.
translation_ko: 걔한텐 비밀 절대 말하면 안 돼
situation: 입이 가벼운 사람을 경계하라고 말할 때
nuance: the last person you'd want to ~ = 가장 ~하고 싶지 않은 사람.
example_1: He's the last person I'd trust with money.
example_2: That's the last thing I expected to hear.

expression: There's nothing wrong with looking for a new job.
translation_ko: 새 직장 알아보는 게 잘못은 아니야
situation: 어떤 행동이 잘못이 아니라고 안심시킬 때
nuance: there's nothing wrong with -ing = ~해도 아무 문제 없다. 정당화나 위로에 쓴다.
example_1: There's nothing wrong with asking for help.
example_2: There's nothing wrong with taking your time.

expression: There's nothing wrong with doing the right thing.
translation_ko: 옳은 일을 하는 게 뭐가 잘못이야
situation: 바른 행동을 망설이는 사람을 격려할 때
nuance: do the right thing = 옳은 일을 하다. 도덕적 선택을 응원하는 표현.
example_1: There's nothing wrong with being honest.
example_2: You did the right thing by telling the truth.

expression: They rushed into buying the house without even seeing it in person.
translation_ko: 직접 보지도 않고 성급하게 집을 샀더라
situation: 누가 성급하게 큰 결정을 내렸다고 말할 때
nuance: rush into = 성급히 ~에 뛰어들다. without even -ing = ~조차 하지 않고.
example_1: Don't rush into signing the contract.
example_2: They got married without even telling their families.

expression: This app makes cooking easy.
situation: 어떤 것이 일을 쉽게 만들어 준다고 말할 때
nuance: make + 목적어 + 형용사 = ~을 …하게 만들다. 사역동사 make 의 기본형.
example_1: Music makes long drives bearable.
example_2: This tool makes editing so much faster.

expression: Tipping your server is an American thing.
translation_ko: 종업원한테 팁 주는 건 미국 문화야
situation: 문화 차이를 설명할 때
nuance: server = (식당) 종업원. a ~ thing 으로 특정 문화의 특성을 짚는다.
example_1: Bowing when you greet someone is a Korean thing.
example_2: Is afternoon tea a British thing?

expression: Think in English.
situation: 영어 학습 방법을 조언할 때
nuance: think in + 언어 = 그 언어로 사고하다. 한국어로 번역하지 말고 바로 그 언어로 떠올리라는 뜻.
example_1: Try to think in English instead of translating.
example_2: Once you start dreaming in a language, you're really fluent.

expression: What's done is done.
situation: 되돌릴 수 없는 일을 받아들일 때
nuance: 관용구. 후회 대신 '끝난 건 끝난 거'라며 받아들이는 태도를 보인다.
example_1: What's done is done — let's focus on what's next.
example_2: There's no point worrying now; what's done is done.

expression: What took you so long?
situation: 한참 기다린 뒤 상대에게 가볍게 핀잔을 줄 때
nuance: what took (you) so long = 뭐 때문에 오래 걸렸냐. 가벼운 불평이나 농담.
example_1: What took you so long at the store?
example_2: You're finally here — what took you so long?

expression: You're used to that reaction.
situation: 어떤 반응이나 상황에 이미 익숙하다고 말할 때
nuance: be used to + 명사/-ing = ~에 익숙하다. 과거 습관의 used to + 동사원형과 구별.
example_1: I'm used to working late.
example_2: You'll get used to the noise.

expression: You made a big mess when you mixed up the files.
situation: 누가 실수로 일을 엉망으로 만들었을 때
nuance: make a mess = 엉망으로 만들다. mix up = 헷갈려서 뒤섞다.
example_1: Don't make a mess in the kitchen.
example_2: I mixed up their names — so embarrassing.

expression: I'm thinking about accepting the job offer.
translation_ko: 그 일자리 제안 받아들일까 고민 중이야
situation: 아직 결정하지 않은 일을 두고 고민할 때
nuance: be thinking about -ing = ~할까 생각 중이다. 아직 미정인 고려를 나타낸다.
example_1: I'm thinking about moving to Busan.
example_2: She's thinking about going back to school.

expression: I'll get my CFO to join us.
situation: 회의나 자리에 다른 사람을 불러 참여시키겠다고 할 때
nuance: get someone to ~ = ~하도록 시키다/하게 하다. make 보다 부드러운 사역.
example_1: I'll get someone to fix it.
example_2: Can you get him to call me?

expression: Let's set up a lunch with his client.
translation_ko: 그쪽 고객이랑 점심 자리 한번 잡자
situation: 미팅이나 약속을 잡자고 제안할 때
nuance: set up = (자리·미팅을) 마련하다/잡다. work lunch = 업무상 점심.
example_1: Let's set up a call for Monday.
example_2: I set up a meeting with the team.

expression: We have a contract.
situation: 계약이나 약속을 근거로 자기 입장을 말할 때
nuance: 간단하지만 단호한 한마디. 협상이나 항의에서 근거로 쓴다.
example_1: We have a deal, remember?
example_2: Do we have an agreement?

expression: We need the conference room.
situation: 공간이나 자원이 필요하다고 요청할 때
nuance: need = 필요하다(직접적). 업무 요청에서 간결하게 쓴다.
example_1: We need more time to finish this.
example_2: I need the report by noon.

expression: I'll get the staff to help you find the right size.
translation_ko: 직원분이 맞는 사이즈 찾는 걸 도와드리게 할게요
situation: 매장에서 직원을 통해 손님을 돕겠다고 할 때
nuance: get someone to help = ~가 돕게 하다. 서비스 상황의 정중한 표현.
example_1: I'll get a colleague to walk you through it.
example_2: Let me get the manager to assist you.

expression: What brings you here?
situation: 뜻밖의 장소에서 만난 사람에게 이유를 물을 때
nuance: 직역 '무엇이 너를 데려왔니'가 곧 '어쩐 일'. Why are you here? 보다 부드럽고 정중하다.
example_1: What brings you to Seoul?
example_2: So, what brings you in today?

expression: What inspired you to create a unisex fragrance?
translation_ko: 유니섹스 향수를 만들게 된 계기가 뭐예요?
situation: 인터뷰나 대화에서 어떤 일을 시작한 동기를 물을 때
nuance: what inspired you to ~ = 무엇이 ~하게 영감을 줬나/계기가 됐나. 세련된 질문 표현.
example_1: What inspired you to start your own business?
example_2: What made you decide to move abroad?

expression: When you travel, the last thing you want is to lose your passport.
translation_ko: 여행할 땐 여권 잃어버리는 게 제일 끔찍해
situation: 여행 중 가장 피하고 싶은 일을 말할 때
nuance: the last thing you want = 가장 원치 않는 것. 여행 상황에서 단골로 쓰인다.
example_1: The last thing you want on a flight is a dead phone.
example_2: Getting sick abroad is the last thing anyone wants.
